claims.text: A thin, continuous aluminide coating on zirconium-alloy cladding will improve resistance to high-temperature steam oxidation.
The aluminide coating converts to a dense Al2O3 scale during high-temperature steam oxidation.
The coating can retain the mechanical and thermal suitability of zirconium-alloy cladding during service.
A few-micrometre aluminide layer can be deposited on zirconium-alloy cladding by pack cementation or chemical vapor deposition.
Under high-temperature service conditions, the aluminide layer reacts with oxygen to form a protective alumina scale.
A continuous, dense, and adherent alumina scale limits oxygen ingress by acting as a diffusion barrier.
The aluminide layer oxidizes preferentially relative to the underlying zirconium alloy in high-temperature steam.
The resulting alumina scale is slow-growing and has a high melting point.
The alumina scale inhibits rapid oxidation of the underlying zirconium alloy.
Inhibiting oxidation of the zirconium alloy mitigates the exothermic zirconium-steam reaction and hydrogen production.
Untreated or normally passivated zirconium-alloy cladding undergoes rapid oxidation and hydrogen generation in high-temperature steam.
At approximately 1200 degrees Celsius for approximately one hour in steam, aluminide-coated cladding will have lower weight gain than uncoated cladding.
At approximately 1200 degrees Celsius for approximately one hour in steam, aluminide-coated cladding will exhibit shallower oxide penetration than uncoated cladding.
The alumina scale will retard oxygen diffusion into the zirconium-alloy substrate.
The protective effect depends on the aluminide coating being uniform, properly adherent, and of controlled thickness.
Excessive coating thickness or poor processing can cause deleterious interdiffusion or embrittlement.
The optimum coating thickness and deposition parameters needed to combine alumina formation with acceptable mechanical and thermal properties are uncertain.
Long-term coating behavior under irradiation and cyclic thermal stress has not been established.
